purpose: Define evidence required to progress from deterministic simulation to actuator-disabled HIL, supervised low-energy trials, and bounded live operation without treating simulator metrics as physical safety proof.

condition_definitions.hazard_register: Every identified hazard has a severity, operating mode, mitigation, verification method, owner, and residual-risk decision.
condition_definitions.deterministic_safety_authority: Geofence, proximity, occupancy, stale-data, emergency-stop, approval, watchdog, policy, and revision checks remain independent of learned output.
condition_definitions.model_cannot_issue_permits: Model bytes and predictions cannot grant authority, lower severity, invoke an adapter, or self-promote.
condition_definitions.immutable_configuration_identity: Topology, policy, model, adapter, firmware, simulator, and evidence identities are digest-bound.
condition_definitions.scenario_falsification: Systematic parameter sweeps and counterexample-directed simulation cover nominal, boundary, misuse, and compound-hazard cases.
condition_definitions.fault_injection_and_replay: Omission, frozen, delayed, inverted, oscillating, corrupted, replayed, stale, bus-off, stuck-actuator, watchdog, and emergency-stop faults are reproducible.
condition_definitions.deadline_freshness_and_liveliness: Observation age, command deadline, sequence, clock uncertainty, transport lifespan, and source liveliness fail closed.
condition_definitions.actuator_disabled_hil_path: The full permit and delivery path can be exercised while actuator execution is structurally unavailable.
condition_definitions.application_risk_assessment: The exact robot application and reasonably foreseeable misuse receive a documented lifecycle risk assessment; generic Ferrum tests are insufficient.
condition_definitions.measured_hardware_timing: Real controller, sensor, network, and adapter latency/jitter are measured under representative and worst-case load against declared deadlines.
condition_definitions.measured_stopping_performance: Worst-case protective-stop time and distance are measured for the exact robot, payload, speed, controller, tooling, and environment.
condition_definitions.contact_force_pressure_assessed: Human-contact force and pressure are measured with an appropriate method, or a documented risk assessment proves contact is excluded and the condition inapplicable.
condition_definitions.independent_emergency_stop: A physical emergency-stop and energy-removal path is demonstrated independently of Ferrum, the learned model, and ordinary networking.
condition_definitions.safety_control_performance_verified: Safety-related control functions are validated to the application-required performance level or integrity target by competent assessors.
condition_definitions.representative_robot_trials: The exact configuration completes predeclared nominal, boundary, fault, misuse, recovery, and update-regression trials with raw logs and no unresolved critical hazards.
condition_definitions.independent_safety_assessment: A technically, managerially, and financially independent competent party reviews the safety case, implementation, raw evidence, residual risk, and claim scope.
condition_definitions.post_update_regression_plan: Each model, policy, firmware, topology, tool, or controller change has impact analysis, evidence invalidation rules, and required regression tests.

model_boundary_challenge.decision_rule: If every gate passes, retain the checkpoint and record that retraining is not justified by this challenge. If any gate fails, register a new train/validation/test protocol before fitting a replacement.

primary_sources.use: lifecycle hazard identification, risk assessment, risk reduction, documentation and verification
industrial robot safety requirements and foreseeable misuse boundary
application integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance and decommissioning
collaborative operation, monitored stop, speed/separation monitoring and power/force limiting
contact force and pressure measurement methods
safety-related control-system design and integration methodology
claim-based safety case combining analysis, simulation, closed-course and operational evidence
repeatable apparatus, procedure, metric and exact-configuration reporting
deadline, lifespan and liveliness transport conditions
measured deadline latency/jitter and avoidance of nondeterministic control-path operations
simulation-guided falsification, systematic fuzzing, counterexample analysis and dataset augmentation
probabilistic scenario distributions for rare-event training and test generation
systematic software safety and independent verification and validation lifecycle

limitations: This protocol is an engineering checklist informed by sources; it is not a statement of ISO, IEC, UL, NIST, NASA or ROS compliance.
Applicability and required performance levels depend on the exact robot, application, jurisdiction and hazards.
Simulation falsification can find counterexamples but cannot prove physical safety.
No current repository artifact satisfies the external HIL, robot-trial or independent-assessment conditions.
